story.value: The name rubidium comes from the Latin word rubidus, meaning deepest red, because of the two deep red lines in its spectra.
Rubidium was discovered in 1861 by the German chemists Robert Bunsen and Gustav Kirchhoff while studying samples of the mineral lepidolite.

uses.value: Rubidium is used in vacuum tubes as a getter, a material that combines with and removes trace gases from the tubes.
Rubidium is used as a part of photocells.
Rubidium has been used in making special glasses.
Because rubidium is easily ionized, it might be used as a propellant in ion engines on spacecraft.
